articles.title: 'Westminster is not working': Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland unite against UK rule
articles.description: Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have signed a new cooperation agreement described as an “independence pact,” intensifying debate over the future of the United Kingdom. The agreement calls for closer cooperation among nationalist movements and urges Westminster to prepare for constitutional change. Scotland’s John Swinney highlighted renewed demands for an independence referendum, while Wales’ Rhun ap Iorwerth argued that Westminster is failing to serve the nations effectively. Northern Ireland’s Michelle O’Neill and Sinn Fein leader Mary Lou McDonald also backed the right to self-determination. The development follows Donald Trump’s recent comments supporting Irish reunification, adding fresh pressure to an already sensitive constitutional debate.

articles.title: MBS arm-twists Trump for help as Houthis rain missiles on Saudi: US says no, offers this instead...
articles.description: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has held talks with U.S. Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper in Jeddah amid escalating Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. The Saudi Press Agency said the meeting reviewed Saudi-U.S. relations and the latest regional developments. It came days after the crown prince reportedly asked President Donald Trump for direct U.S. military action against Yemen’s Houthi movement. Reuters reported that Washington declined to take direct military action for now, but agreed to support Riyadh with intelligence-sharing and targeting assistance. The U.S. support is also reported to include advice on Saudi air-defence strategy as the kingdom faces continuing aerial threats to cities, energy sites and key Red Sea approaches.

articles.title: Explosions near Israel border: What really happened at Jordan’s strategic Red Sea port city of Aqaba?
articles.description: Explosions and an ammonia gas leak have triggered alarm in Aqaba, Jordan, raising questions amid heightened regional tensions. At least 11 people were reportedly injured after an incident in the industrial area of the key Red Sea port city. Jordanian authorities said the leak occurred during maintenance work involving an old pump or pressure equipment and was contained. Workers are expected to return only after safety inspections and measurements are completed. The incident was not immediately attributed to an attack. Aqaba lies near the borders with Israel, Saudi Arabia and Egypt, making any industrial emergency particularly sensitive as tensions remain high across the region.

articles.title: In 1997, a Western Australian coal mine closed; its 103-hectare void filled with about 30 billion litres of water and opened in 2020 as Lake Kepwari
articles.description: Lake Kepwari, a former coal mine void near Collie, Western Australia, has been transformed into a recreational hub. This artificial lake now offers swimming, boating, camping, and water sports for visitors. The transformation involved significant planning, water management, and infrastructure development over many years. Water was diverted from the Collie River South Branch to fill the large void. This project demonstrates repurposing industrial landscapes for tourism and community benefit.

articles.title: Symbiosis Recovers 15 BTC Following Attack on syBTC Minting
articles.description: Symbiosis recovered around 15 BTC after an attacker exploited a flaw in its Bitcoin Bridge on September 11. The protocol suspended native Bitcoin routes and isolated the affected bridge while keeping other cross-chain routes operational. Symbiosis has not disclosed the total loss and is still assessing the impact on liquidity providers.
